task.description: WF-02 Step 2c HARD GATE: security review of the new search/2 function added to lib/letflow/definitions.ex (branch feature/WF02-REQ042-20260817, diff git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions.ex). This is a tenant-scoped free-text read query built with fragment/1 CASE and ILIKE expressions -- the highest-risk surface for SQL injection this project has shipped so far. Verify the '%' wildcard composition and every fragment SQL-text argument extremely carefully.
acceptance_criteria: Scope test performed: confirm this diff touches a tenant-data path
For each of INV-1..INV-8: determine APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE with reasoning
For each APPLIES invariant, the verification check actually run (not asserted)

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) gets the deepest scrutiny: every fragment/1 call's first argument must be a fixed compile-time string literal, with only bound ^-pinned values or column references as placeholders -- confirm the query string itself never reaches raw SQL text (including the '%' wildcard composition: pattern = "%" <> query <> "%" must be composed into the bound VALUE, not the fragment SQL text)

Specific check: search/2 never accepts or trusts a caller-supplied tenant_id -- tenant scoping comes entirely from opts[:prefix] -> TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1, same pattern as create/2, get_by_id/2, list/2
Specific check: no cross-tenant data leak -- confirm the Ecto query is scoped via prefix: prefix on the Repo.all/2 call, same as the rest of this module

result.summary: Scope test: APPLIES (tenant-data path) -- search/2 is a new read query against process_definitions, a tenant-scoped table, added in lib/letflow/definitions.ex. Diff verified against the correct base (local `main` ref was stale vs origin/main -- REQ-042's actual own diff, `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/`, is 149 lines in definitions.ex plus the new search.md design doc; zero migrations touched, confirming the moduledoc's 'zero new priv/repo/migrations/ files' claim). `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` succeeds (exit 0). Every fragment/1 call added by this diff (where_search_match/2 line 698, select_with_rank/3 line 717-724, order_by_rank/3 line 732-739) has a first argument that is a fixed compile-time string literal written directly in source -- confirmed by direct read, not just grep: "? ILIKE ? OR ? ILIKE ?" and "CASE WHEN lower(?) = lower(?) THEN 3.0 WHEN ? ILIKE ? THEN 2.0 ELSE 1.0 END". Every ? placeholder in those literals binds to either a column reference (d.name, d.description) or a ^-pinned Elixir value (^pattern, ^search_query) -- confirmed no <> or #{} construction feeds any fragment SQL-text argument (grep -B3 fragment( shows only `pattern = "%" <> query <> "%"` above where_name/2, an unrelated sibling helper for list/2, and no concatenation adjacent to search/2's three fragment calls). The '%' wildcard composition happens entirely in Elixir (line 537, `pattern = "%" <> query <> "%"`) and pattern is passed only as the bound value ^pattern -- the wildcard characters never appear inside any fragment SQL-text literal. grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/ priv/repo/migrations/ shows 5 existing hits, none touched by this diff, none in definitions.ex, and all pre-existing schema-name-interpolation patterns already covered by prior security reviews outside this scope. search/2's opts type (search_opts :: [prefix, limit, offset]) has no tenant_id key at all -- tenant scoping is derived exclusively via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix) (called only for validation, matching create/2/get_by_id/2/get_active_by_name/2/list/2's identical pattern) and the query itself is scoped via `Repo.all(ecto_query, prefix: prefix)` -- same schema-per-tenant mechanism as every other function in this module, no tenant_id column filter used (consistent with list/2, which relies on schema-prefix isolation alone per decision 0003 Dimension B). No bare `{:ok, _} = ` pattern matches introduced (grep clean); search/2 uses a `with` chain throughout, same idiom as create/2 and list/2. INV-4 heuristic secret greps produced no hits attributable to this diff. All INV-1/4/6/7/8 checks pass; INV-2/3/5 remain correctly NOT-APPLICABLE (S4/S5 not started, and search/2 is a context-module function, not an HTTP lookup-by-ID or response-serialisation surface).

(b) No priv/repo/migrations/ file touched by this diff (confirmed via git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- lib/letflow/ priv/repo/migrations/ -- only lib/letflow/definitions.ex and lib/letflow/design/search.md changed), so no table is newly left reachable outside the prefix mechanism. (c) N/A for this function specifically -- search/2 performs no INSERT/UPDATE and never touches a tenant_id column at all; it does not accept :tenant_id in opts (search_opts type has only prefix/limit/offset) so there is no caller-supplied value that could disagree with the resolved schema.

Ecto is in use; search/2 introduces three new fragment/1 calls carrying user-controlled query text -- the highest-scrutiny check for this review.
invariant_table.verification: Direct read of all three fragment/1 call sites (definitions.ex:698, 717-724, 732-739): first argument in every case is a fixed compile-time string literal ("? ILIKE ? OR ? ILIKE ?" and "CASE WHEN lower(?) = lower(?) THEN 3.0 WHEN ? ILIKE ? THEN 2.0 ELSE 1.0 END"), never built via <> or #{}. Every ? placeholder binds to a column reference (d.name, d.description) or a ^-pinned value (^pattern, ^search_query) -- Ecto compiles these to genuine bound Postgres parameters. The '%' wildcard composition (pattern = "%" <> query <> "%", line 537) happens entirely in Elixir and produces a bound VALUE passed as ^pattern -- confirmed the wildcard characters never appear inside any fragment SQL-text literal. grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/ priv/repo/migrations/ --include=*.ex --include=*.exs shows 5 hits, all pre-existing (sandbox_pool.ex, tenant_provisioning.ex, sandbox_pool/fixture_loader.ex) and none touched by this diff or reachable from search/2.

invariant_table.verification: grep -rn "^\s*{:ok, .*} = " lib/letflow/definitions.ex -- zero hits. search/2 uses a `with` chain (check_query_not_empty/1, check_query_not_too_long/1, TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1) with every clause returning a typed :ok/:error tuple, same idiom as create/2, get_by_id/2, list/2. No bare pattern match that can raise on realistic (including malformed/oversized/adversarial) query input.
